about: The signed transfer offer the plugin publishes to a device on the native call surface (voice_system_ui) has a derived id, so that a ring hint, if a host posts one, and the offer the phone later receives name the same offer and the phone upgrades its placeholder in place instead of ringing twice. No host posts a ring hint yet: the id is defined here and vector-tested, and the plugin publishes the offer under it. offerId = "toffer_" + lower-case RFC 4648 base32 (no padding) of SHA-256("oaiy/transfer-offer/v1" 0x00 requestId 0x00 holderThumbprint), first 26 characters. holderThumbprint is the device's endpoint-key thumbprint: the base64url SHA-256 of {"crv":"Ed25519","kty":"OKP","x":<base64url public key>}. A retired offer is never published again under the same id, because the phone spends an offer before it answers: generation 0 hashes as above and generation n >= 1 appends 0x00 and the decimal n to the hashed input. The plugin increments a per (request, holder) counter whenever it retires that offer; a refresh of an unanswered offer keeps the id and takes a fresh jti. A ring hint would carry generation 0. The id is an identifier, never a credential: the offer's signed token and one-use jti authorise anything. Two devices that present the same key derive the same id; the first keeps it.
